definitions.text: Uses cocaine, methamphetamine or misused stimulant pills in binges, more than planned.
Has strong cravings and crashes with exhaustion and low mood after use.
Use has caused health, money, work or legal problems, or periods of paranoia.

longTermGoals.text: The client reaches their own goal for stimulant use, stays safer from overdose and health harm, and rebuilds daily routines.

shortTermObjectives.text: Within 2 weeks, enroll in a program that offers contingency management, if available.
By the next session, have naloxone available, because the drug supply may contain fentanyl.
By session 3, set a personal use goal and list 3 reasons for change.
Use a coping skill for at least 3 cravings a week and record the outcome.
By session 8, complete a relapse prevention plan with high-risk situations, coping steps and support contacts.

collaborativeNote: Write goals and objectives with the client in their own words. Timelines and targets are examples to adapt; the client decides what matters, and the clinician checks safety and fit. Every item in this plan records substance use: the export carries the 42 CFR Part 2 notice.
